topic.title: Network Communities and Statistical Graph Structure
topic.area: Graphical Models, Clustering, and Network Structure
topic.overview: Community detection seeks groups of nodes with distinctive connection patterns. This topic studies graph clustering through stochastic block models, spectral methods, random walks, and related network statistics. A representative recovery algorithm uses singular-value decomposition to handle communities of unequal sizes, with guarantees that explicitly address the presence of many small groups.
topic.whyItMatters: Real networks rarely consist of balanced, isolated communities. Understanding detectability limits and model assumptions helps explain when a partition reflects recoverable structure and when an algorithm may miss smaller or overlapping groups.
topic.evolution: The representatives begin with web communities and spectral subgraph detection, then expand to evolving, correlated, sparse, and hypergraph networks. Recent work includes bipartite community detection and block-model testing. Signed-graph estimation adds a related computational thread concerned with positive and negative network relationships.
openQuestions: How can methods reveal small communities without overinterpreting noise?
Which recovery guarantees survive temporal changes, overlap, or departures from block-model assumptions?
